text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Denmark's Central Bank is to issue fewer government bonds in 1997 creating greater demand and lowering yields for the benefit of the Danish bond market.

--- Denmark's postal service is to cooperate with other Scandinavian post offices in competing with private courier companies. At present the Danish post service has 10-15 percent of the domestic market for business parcels, but is now aiming for a 50 percent market share.

--- British cut-price airline Virgin Express is to lower prices on flights from Copenhagen via Brussels to seven European cities with the aim of upping passenger figures on its Copenhagen-Brussels route.
--- Pump manufacturing group Danfoss says the bulk of its research and development activities will be moved abroad in the next decade due to a shortage in Denmark of qualified engineers.

--- 32 percent of all Danish companies expect to employ academic graduates within the next five years, more than a doubling compared to 1994 when only 14.4 percent of firms did so, according to a new survey.
